strings.text: PERFECT POUR · {recipe} — IN THE BOOK NOW
strings.note: Gold toast under the top bar the first time a recipe is poured perfectly. {recipe} = the drink's name in capitals. One line, ~60 characters at display 14.

strings.text: NEVER SHAKEN · BUILT AT THE GLASS
strings.note: Red warning row on the cellar's bottle card for a fizzy bottle, beside a no-shake icon. One line, 16px body face, ~34 characters.

Second row of the garnish card over a rim dish on the counter (salt/sugar rim). {word} = the dish's short verb caption from the counter rail, already in capitals. One line, 16px body face, ~30 characters. Keep the two spaces either side of the dot.
Second row of the garnish card over the ice bucket. {word} = the bucket's short caption, already in capitals. One line, 16px body face, ~30 characters.
Second row of the garnish card over a garnish dish (lime, olive...). {word} = the dish's short caption, already in capitals. One line, 16px body face, ~30 characters.
Price row on the garnish card, after a yellow $ sign. {price} = whole dollars (digits only). One line, display face 16, ~12 characters.
Price row on the cellar's bottle card, after a yellow $ sign. {price} = whole dollars (digits only). One line, display face 16, ~14 characters.
Price row on the garnish card for something that costs nothing (ice, free garnish), after a yellow $ sign. One line, display face 16, ~14 characters.
Second row of the cellar's bottle card, under the bottle's name. {style} = the bottle's style in capitals (e.g. LONDON DRY), {tier} = quality rung 1-5. One line, 16px body face, ~30 characters.
Stock row on the cellar/garnish card, above a fill bar. {left} = amount remaining with one decimal (e.g. 12.5), {capacity} = the full amount, whole number. One line, 16px body face, ~24 characters.
The same stock row, in red, when 15% or less is left. {left} = amount remaining with one decimal, {capacity} = the full amount, whole number. One line, 16px body face, ~40 characters.
Heading on the cellar's bottle card over the list of house drinks (icon + name) that use this bottle. One line, 16px body face, ~20 characters.
The same heading when the list is cut at six drinks. {n} = how many more drinks are not listed. One line, 16px body face, ~30 characters.
As chrome.cellar.uses_more#one.
The same heading when no drink on the player's menu uses this bottle (the list under it is empty). One line, 16px body face, ~24 characters.
Name plate under a run of bottles on the cellar shelf: the family they belong to. 8px body face on a plate as wide as the word; keep it short, ~12 characters.
Cellar shelf family plate, as chrome.cellar.group.gin. ~12 characters.
Cellar shelf family plate, as chrome.cellar.group.gin. ~12 characters.
Cellar shelf family plate for whisky/whiskey, as chrome.cellar.group.gin. ~12 characters.
Cellar shelf family plate, as chrome.cellar.group.gin. ~12 characters.
Cellar shelf family plate, as chrome.cellar.group.gin. ~12 characters.
Cellar shelf family plate for cocktail bitters, as chrome.cellar.group.gin. ~12 characters.
Cellar shelf family plate for sweet syrups, as chrome.cellar.group.gin. ~12 characters.
Cellar shelf family plate for fruit juices, as chrome.cellar.group.gin. ~12 characters.
Cellar shelf family plate for sour mixers that are not juice, as chrome.cellar.group.gin. ~12 characters.
Cellar shelf family plate for fizzy mixers (soda water, tonic, cola), as chrome.cellar.group.gin. ~12 characters.
Cellar shelf family plate for any other mixer, as chrome.cellar.group.gin. ~12 characters.
Where a bought fitting stands, on a market card, when its slot is on the bar counter. Fills {place} in chrome.rung.place_pair / place_over. Sentence case, ~16 characters.
Where a bought fitting stands, on a market card, when its slot is on the wall behind the bar. Fills {place} in chrome.rung.place_pair / place_over. Sentence case, ~16 characters.

Market card line for an upgrade rung that comes as a matching pair (two wall lamps). {place} = where it stands (The counter / The back wall / a place name from the data). One line, small body face, ~40 characters.

Market card line for an upgrade rung that replaces the lower rung in the same spot. {place} = where it stands (The counter / The back wall / a place name from the data). One line, small body face, ~40 characters.
Caption in the night's well on the top bar once the bar is calling time, in magenta. Replaces the crowd word. 8px display face, ~14 characters.
Caption in the night's well on the top bar: tonight's crowd is wealthy. 8px display face, ~14 characters.
Caption in the night's well on the top bar: tonight's crowd has little money. 8px display face, ~14 characters.
Caption in the night's well on the top bar: an ordinary crowd tonight. 8px display face, ~14 characters.

Lime toast when the week's job is finished and paid. {who} = the job giver's name in capitals (e.g. ECE), {reward} = whole dollars, digits only (the $ is in the text). One line, ~30 characters at display 14.

Line in the service log (the LOG sheet, top left) when the week's job is finished. Keep the <color> tags around the job's name. {who} = the giver's name in capitals, {reward} = whole dollars, digits only. One line, 8px body face, ~40 characters.

The week's job strip under the top bar (a small plate beside the LOG key): what the job counts when it asks for perfect pours. Shown after the giver's name and a count like 2/5. 8px display face, ~16 characters.
The week's job strip: what the job counts when it asks for nights closed with a clean counter. Shown after the giver's name and a count like 2/5. 8px display face, ~16 characters.

The week's job strip once the job is finished, all in lime. {who} = the giver's name in capitals, {target} = how many were asked for (printed twice as n/n), {reward} = whole dollars, digits only. One line, 8px display face, ~34 characters.
Caption on the small key under the top bar's left end that opens the service log. Key is 44x20, 8px body face: ~5 characters at most.
Service log: stands in for the drink's name when the glass served matches no recipe; fills {drink} in chrome.log.why_made. 8px body face, ~14 characters.
Service log, a reason in brackets after a WRONG serve. {drink} = the drink actually made, in capitals, or NOTHING NAMED. Lower case; one of a comma-separated list, ~24 characters.
Service log, a reason in brackets after a CLOSE serve: the right drink with the proportions out. Lower case; one of a comma-separated list, ~14 characters.
Service log, a reason in brackets: how well the serving spec (ice, garnish, rim) was met. {pct} = a percentage already formatted with its % sign (e.g. 50%). Lower case, ~12 characters.
Service log, a reason in brackets: how full the glass was. {pct} = a percentage already formatted with its % sign (e.g. 80%). Lower case, ~12 characters.
Service log verdict word at the start of a serve's line, in green: the drink they ordered, made right. 8px body face, ~8 characters.
Service log verdict word at the start of a serve's line, in amber: their drink, but the measures were off. Not the verb 'to close'. 8px body face, ~8 characters.
Service log verdict word at the start of a serve's line, in red: a different drink from the one ordered. 8px body face, ~8 characters.
Title of the settings window, beside the cog in its dark title band. Display face 16, ~20 characters.
Settings window: small amber group caption over the volume and sound rows. 8px body face, ~20 characters.
Settings row label (left side); a -/+ pair and a five-block meter sit on the right. 16px body face, ~16 characters.
Settings: the volume as a percentage, small, left of the meter. {pct} = 0 to 100, digits only. Move the % sign where your language writes it. ~5 characters.
Settings row label: turns all sound on or off with the key on the right (ON / OFF). 16px body face, ~16 characters.
Caption on the SOUND row's toggle key while sound plays. Key is 96x28, 8px body face, ~10 characters.
Caption on the SOUND row's toggle key while sound is muted. Key is 96x28, 8px body face, ~10 characters.
Settings window: small amber group caption over the motion row. 8px body face, ~20 characters.
Settings row label: full or reduced animation, toggled by the key on the right (FULL / REDUCED). 16px body face, ~16 characters.

strings.text: REDUCED: NO SLIDES, NO FLOATS, NO FADES
strings.note: Small note under the MOTION row label explaining what REDUCED turns off. One line, 8px body face, ~40 characters.
Caption on the MOTION row's toggle key when every animation plays. Key is 96x28, 8px body face, ~10 characters.
Caption on the MOTION row's toggle key when slides, floats and fades are off. Key is 96x28, 8px body face, ~10 characters.
Settings row label: picks the game's language with the ◀ ▶ keys on the right, which show each language's own name. 16px body face, ~16 characters.

Small note under LANGUAGE, shown only after the player picks a different language, and shown IN the picked language: the game switches when it is started again. One line, 8px body face, ~34 characters.
Settings window: small amber group caption over the book and new-run rows (the current playthrough). 8px body face, ~20 characters.
Settings row label: opens the register's ledger of past nights. 16px body face, ~18 characters.

strings.text: EVERY LINE THE TILL HAS TAKEN
strings.note: Small note under TONIGHT'S BOOK. One line, 8px body face, ~34 characters.
Caption on the key that opens tonight's book (the ledger). Key is 96x28, 8px body face, ~10 characters.
Settings row label: throw the current run away and start a new one. 16px body face, ~18 characters.

strings.text: DAY 1, AN EMPTY BAR — THIS NIGHT IS LOST
strings.note: Small warning note under START OVER. One line, 8px body face, ~40 characters.
Caption on the red key that starts a new run from day 1. Key is 96x28, 8px body face, ~10 characters.
Caption on a window's close key (settings window foot, ledger foot). Keys are 120-200 wide and 32-38 tall, 16px body face, ~12 characters.
Caption on the story plate's listen key (the plate at the bottom where the host or the last customer speaks, face and name on the left): shows the next line. Key fits ~12 characters.
Caption on the story plate's listen key on the last line of the last customer's ask: closes the talk and starts the pouring. ~12 characters.
Caption on the story plate's listen key on the last line when the guest leaves because the bar has not earned enough stars yet. ~12 characters.
Caption on the story plate's listen key on the last line of one of the host's lessons (a tutorial tip). ~12 characters.

strings.text: COMES BACK AT {need} STARS  ·  YOU HAVE {now}
strings.note: Row under the story plate while a guest explains they will return later: the star rating they need and the bar's rating now. {need} and {now} = ratings with one decimal (e.g. 3.5). One line, ~44 characters.

Post-it beside the bar while pouring the last customer's round: which drink of how many, and how many mistakes are still allowed. {at} = the drink being made (1-based), {total} = drinks asked for, {n} = mistakes left. One line, ~24 characters.
As chrome.story.count_spare#one.
The same post-it when the round allows no mistakes. {at} = the drink being made (1-based), {total} = drinks asked for. One line, ~28 characters.

Warning on the last customer's post-it when the bar lacks a bottle the current drink needs. {styles} = the missing bottle styles in capitals, comma-separated (e.g. LONDON DRY, BOURBON). One line, ~40 characters.

strings.text: YOU TOLD THEM NO — THEY WILL BE BACK
strings.note: Toast after the player declines the last customer's request for tonight. One line, ~40 characters at display 14.
Title of the ledger window (opened from Settings > TONIGHT'S BOOK): every closed night's money. Display face 16, one line, ~34 characters.

strings.text: DAY        TOOK        PAID OUT         NET        TILL
strings.note: Column header over the ledger's rows, in a monospace pixel face: the words sit over the columns of chrome.ledger.row_head (day, money taken, money paid out, net, till). Keep each word starting at the same character position as the English; the line holds ~56 characters.

strings.text: No days yet. Close a night first.
strings.note: Shown alone on the ledger's page before any night has been closed. Sentence case, one line, ~40 characters.

First line of a night in the ledger, aligned under the column header. {day} = day number padded to 3, {income} = money taken padded to 7, {expenses} = money paid out padded to 8, {net} = +$n or -$n padded to 8, {till} = $n left in the till (may be empty). Keep the $ signs and the spacing; only DAY is a word.
Second line of an old ledger night saved before details were kept. {mood} = GREAT / OK / SOUR (chrome.mood.*). Lower case after the mood, one line, ~40 characters.
Ledger money line item: what the drinks were charged. {amount} = whole dollars, digits only. Items are joined with ' · '. Lower case, ~16 characters.
Ledger money line item: tips taken. {amount} = whole dollars, digits only. Lower case, ~16 characters.
Ledger money line item: bonus money given as thanks (e.g. for showing a troublemaker the door). {amount} = whole dollars, digits only. Lower case, ~16 characters.
Ledger money line item after the dash: the night's rent. {amount} = whole dollars, digits only. Lower case, ~16 characters.
Ledger money line item after the dash: spent restocking bottles. {amount} = whole dollars, digits only. Lower case, ~16 characters.
Ledger money line item after the dash: spent on bar upgrades (furniture, lights). {amount} = whole dollars, digits only. Lower case, ~16 characters.
Ledger money line item after the dash: fines paid (serving minors, wrong kicks). {amount} = whole dollars, digits only. Lower case, ~16 characters.
Ledger room line item: customers served that night. {n} = a whole number. Items are joined with ' · '. Lower case, ~16 characters.
As chrome.ledger.served#one.
Ledger room line item: customers who left without getting a drink. {n} = a whole number. Lower case, ~24 characters.
As chrome.ledger.walked_out#one.
Ledger room line item when every customer got a drink. Lower case, ~24 characters.
Ledger room line item: customers rightly thrown out that night. {n} = a whole number. Lower case, ~24 characters.
As chrome.ledger.kicked#one.
Ledger room line item: the star rating that night earned. {stars} = a rating with one decimal (e.g. 3.5). Lower case, ~28 characters.
How a night went, by customer satisfaction, in the ledger (fills {mood} in chrome.ledger.row_bare and ends the room line). ~8 characters.
How a night went: middling satisfaction. As chrome.mood.great. ~8 characters.
How a night went: poor satisfaction, customers unhappy. As chrome.mood.great. ~8 characters.

strings.text: TURN THE GLASS IN THE DISH
strings.note: Instruction beside a picture of a rimmed glass on the garnish card (salt or sugar rim). Wraps inside 200 units, 16px body face; two short lines at most.

strings.text: DROP IT IN BEFORE THE POUR
strings.note: Instruction beside the ice bucket picture on the garnish card. Wraps inside 200 units, 16px body face; two short lines at most.

strings.text: ON THE RIM OR IN THE DRINK
strings.note: Instruction beside a garnish dish picture (lime wedge, olive...) on the garnish card: where the garnish goes. Wraps inside 200 units, 16px body face; two short lines at most.
